header.contentDescription: Gas molecules above a catalytic surface with its adsorption sites drawn in 3D

drawTextAnchored.text: the catalyst surface, with its sites
It holds, it does not push
two molecules adsorb on neighbouring sites and are simply held still, facing each other
in the gas they must collide correctly aligned; on the surface they already are
the site is vacated afterwards, which is why a few grams can process tonnes
Poisoning a catalyst means occupying its sites with something that will not leave.
the trick is holding still, not pushing
